descriptionChirho: Qal stative/participial sense describing physical height, tallness of persons or objects, or loudness of voice — Arabic مُرْتَفِع (murtafi'), عَالٍ ('ālin), Korean 높은 (nopeun), Swahili -refu/-kirefu.
Qal imperfect/perfect/infinitive intransitive sense: to rise, become exalted, be lifted in status or glory — Arabic يَرْتَفِعُ (yartafi'u), Korean 높아지다 (nopajida), Swahili -inuliwa/-inuka.
Qal participial/stative sense applied to God as the Exalted One, expressing divine transcendence — Arabic مُتَعَالٍ (muta'ālin), الْعَلِيُّ (al-'aliyyu), Korean 높으시도다, Swahili -inuliwa.
Qal participial sense with negative moral connotation: arrogant, lifted up in pride — Arabic الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ (al-mutakabbirīn), Korean 교만한 (gyomanhan), Swahili -enye kiburi.
Hifil causative sense of physically lifting, raising, or picking up an object, person, or standard — Arabic رَفَعَ (rafa'a), Korean 들어올리다 (deureo-ollida), Swahili -inua.
Hifil causative sense of exalting a person in rank, honor, or power; making someone great — Arabic رَفَعَ (rafa'a figurative), Korean 높이다 (nopida), Swahili -inua (figurative).
Hifil sense of lifting up as a ritual heave offering (terumah) or voluntary contribution — Arabic قَدَّمَ (qaddama), Korean 바치다 (bachida), Swahili -toa.
Hifil sense of lifting something off or away, removing or carrying away — Arabic أَزالَ (azāla), Korean 제거하다 (jegeo-hada), Swahili -ondoa.
Piel intensive sense of actively praising, extolling, or exalting God or a person; making someone's name great — Arabic عَظَّمَ ('aẓẓama), رَفَّعَ (raffa'a), Korean 높이다 (intensive), Swahili -tukuza.
Hitpael reflexive sense of exalting oneself, magnifying oneself — Arabic يَرْتَفِعُ (reflexive), Korean 높이리라 (self-exaltation), Swahili -jikuza.
Pual/Hofal passive sense of being raised or exalted by another agent — Arabic رُفِعَ (rufi'a), Korean 높여진 (nopyeojin), Swahili -inuliwa.
